Hello,
We are happy for your loyalty and the entire {business_name} team appreciates your trust.

Very bad experience at this hospital.
Extremely high quotes and little concern for my cat's well-being.
My 12-year-old cat was hospitalized twice in one week (second hospitalization following the first) and both times she came home worse, with diarrhea, covered in feces, and had a fever.
On one of the visits, I saw that her paw was very swollen because the IV tape was so tight, and even after I spoke to them, they didn't remove it immediately.
I never received a phone call informing me how she was doing.
I only received updates on absurdly high quotes.
They disregarded my opinion, which was later confirmed as correct by other veterinarians. This 'company's' biggest concern was hospitalization, hospitalization...
A lot of insensitivity on the part of the reception staff.

Hello Rayna,

It's good that they're taking care of my cat who was hit by a car; they're very attentive... it's expensive, but it's good...

I first went to this hospital in June, on recommendation, after my dog ​​was diagnosed with a mast cell tumor. In that situation, I have no complaints: the follow-up was adequate and the treatment went satisfactorily.
Unfortunately, in September, my dog ​​was diagnosed with a second tumor, this time a sarcoma. Given the previous positive experience, I trusted this hospital again and sought out its oncology team once more. However, the follow-up this time was deeply disappointing and revealed a worrying lack of communication, organization, transparency, and sense of responsibility.
My dog ​​underwent a CT scan on September 9, 2026, the results of which were available on September 11. Despite it being an urgent oncological situation, I was not contacted by the hospital. I had to call on September 17 to ask about the results, which had already been available for several days. The reception told me, "Usually it's the owner who calls to ask." I ask, if I had contacted them after 2 months, would everything be okay?
The situation became even more serious when I went to the clinic in person to speak with the person in charge of oncology. I was told that this professional would have contacted me by phone, which is not true. I did not receive any call. I consider it absolutely unacceptable that, in the face of a delicate and urgent situation, false information is given to the guardian instead of acknowledging a communication failure.
As the days went by, there was no surgery scheduled, there was no clear action plan, and I did not feel any effective follow-up or concern for my dog's condition. I had to repeatedly insist to obtain basic information about a diagnosis that required speed, responsibility, and proper follow-up.
A hospital that provides veterinary care, especially in the area of ​​oncology, has a duty to communicate results promptly, explain clinical options, set priorities, and act with a sense of urgency. What I found in this second situation was precisely the opposite: disorganization, lack of transparency, absence of follow-up, and an attitude incompatible with the professionalism expected of a team responsible for the health and life of an animal.
Faced with this lack of response, I was forced to seek another institution. Fortunately, I was able to resolve the situation elsewhere, where I found much more competence, speed, empathy, and respect for the animal and the family.
This experience left me deeply disappointed. Good initial follow-up cannot serve to justify or erase such deficient subsequent action. When an oncological disease and possible surgery are involved, every day can be crucial. The lack of communication and sense of urgency demonstrated in this case is not a simple administrative inconvenience: it is a serious failure in the follow-up of a clinical case that required responsibility and rigor.

I sincerely hope that this hospital will review its procedures, the communication between professionals, and the way it follows up on urgent cases. No pet owner should have to chase after information, insist on answers, or discover on their own initiative that an important result had already been available for days.
My assessment is not based on unrealistic expectations, but on concrete experience. And, in this situation, the hospital clearly failed in the communication, support, and professionalism it should have provided.

We have been here twice. Our first experience was great—the administrator and Dr. Telmo were very attentive, noticed our puppy had a fever, and immediately took care of him while we waited.

Unfortunately, our second visit was a completely different story. The receptionist, Patricia, was incredibly inattentive. Our puppy was crying, shaking in severe pain, and clearly distressed. We asked if a nurse could just glance inside his ear while we waited for our turn, as we felt every second counted. Patricia remained completely indifferent, calmly telling us to just wait. It turns out she is a nurse and could have easily checked to reassure us, but she refused to help. Worse, she kept responding with an inappropriate, dismissive smile while we were visibly anxious and worried.

On the bright side, Dr. Ana Freitas was wonderful. She was highly attentive, did everything she could to help our puppy, and clearly explained all the procedures so we understood what was happening.

Five stars for the veterinary care, but the reception experience with Patricia was deeply disappointing.

4 stars for the entire team, with the exception of one receptionist, who is quite lacking in customer service, I would even say in education.
My cat was hospitalized there the first time, and the entire medical team was incredible, as were the receptionists. Today I had to take my cat there again, and so far, 'everything was fine'. Until almost an hour after I arrived, as the discharge had already been issued, I questioned why and was answered with vague and arrogant responses. A heartfelt thank you to the entire clinical team and this time to Dr. Ana Freitas, who, from the beginning of the discharge to the end, was super attentive and explained everything to me perfectly.
Having a file at that clinic, you can see that I already spent €800 there the first time, and I would have paid more if necessary. Imagine my surprise when I went to pay €165, yes, that's right. I was having trouble with the card for about 3 minutes, even after asking where I could get cash. Even though I had more than half the amount, and as is obvious and everyone noticed, it was a card error. Then, the receptionist today, April 17th, who was receiving payments, after all the arrogance and lack of professionalism with the customer, rudely and nonsensically told me that I would have to pay everything today. Needless to say, I gave 800, now 65, and as far as possible my animals will always have everything they need. In the end, while everyone was commenting on the rudeness of your receptionist, a gentleman came up to me and helped me by using his bank to pay the rest. Because I had already paid more than half in cash due to the embarrassment and bad character of your employee, who, even while listening to the calls and seeing that it was a bank error, decided to be rude to me until the end, even though the problem wasn't the amount at all. But rather that the app wasn't working. I recommend the clinic because they are really good at what they do, but I can't say the same about that receptionist.

Hi Tiago, We're very happy that you're also satisfied ;) Thank you so much for this review!

excellent emergency care provided for our dog
Staff is very kind, professional and patient. Staff spoke in excellent english and I had no issues checking in on Sunday evening for urgent visit.
Thank you for your attention and care for the animals.

Despite the outcome, Marley was very well treated at this clinic.
He was admitted on December 19th as an emergency, with a ruptured tumor in his spleen. He was very lethargic and in pain. The doctor who received us that night, although not from the clinic, took all the necessary steps, telling us that same night that it was a tumor that had burst in his spleen. He was hospitalized for about 5 days, had a CT scan which supposedly showed no metastases, and we proceeded with surgery to remove the spleen and the tumors inside it. The surgery went well, leaving a small scar on his lower abdomen. The cytology revealed that it was a malignant tumor, a hemangiosarcoma. This possibility had already been given to us before the surgery, that it could be malignant, but we tried to do everything for Marley, in case it was benign.
We also had an oncology consultation to see what could be done. The doctor explained everything to us in detail, saying that if chemotherapy were to be done, it would be palliative and not curative, and that Marley could live up to 9 months with chemo and up to 30/40 days after surgery.
The final outcome came about 20 days after the surgery, with the hemangiosarcoma spreading to the liver. On January 11, 2026, we called the clinic and asked to speak to the doctor, in this case the oncologist answered, who told us to bring him in. Realizing that Marley's time was approaching, when we arrived they already had a large, fluffy blanket on the floor to provide the necessary comfort for Marley. He passed away peacefully, surrounded by me and my parents, they let us be with him throughout the entire process and for a few more moments to say goodbye to him. In addition, they gave us a small piece of clay with his paw print. The doctor who attended us was super kind and understanding.

Although the service was expensive and the final bill was very close to 2,000 euros, I don't regret taking him there, even though it's about 30 minutes from my house and there are other hospitals closer, like Animed in S. Cosme (which I only hear bad things about). Marley was very well treated until his final hour, the staff is very loving with the animals.
Thank you for everything you tried to do for Marley!

In an urgent and delicate situation, I found a spectacular team that always helped us through difficulties, whether clinical and/or financial decisions. My cat was hospitalized for a week, which involved surgery that was only performed when there was no other option. It is worth highlighting that during this hospitalization, the sensitivity in sharing information at various times of the day by administrators, nurses, and veterinarians was sublime. They never made me feel that I shouldn't call so often, or at late hours (before going to sleep); they were always available and sensitive to the situation of helplessness in not being able to do anything more than make a simple call. The most important thing in this experience is that I never felt that the service changed according to the professionals on duty, showing equity in clinical quality and as people who also deal with people, and that is very valuable. How many times have we stopped going here or there because person x or y wasn't working? Keep it up! Don't let yourselves be sold to companies that try to monopolize the prices presented to clients and with a quality that leaves much to be desired. Thank you very much! The kitten is recovering very well and continues to be monitored.

My dog ​​was admitted to the Porto Veterinary Hospital (CHV Porto) as an emergency. After they strongly insisted on extensive and extremely expensive tests, I went ahead with everything that was recommended, trusting in the alleged professionalism of the team.
The follow-up was nonexistent. During and after the tests, there was no contact to find out how the animal was doing or how it was recovering from the anesthesia, and my dog ​​was very ill during that period.
The results were only communicated after numerous requests on my part. A prolonged treatment with cortisone was prescribed for a month, without any kind of clinical follow-up. During that entire period, there was not a single call, update, or demonstration of concern for the animal's condition.
I sent several emails directly to the doctor responsible for clinical follow-up, all without any response. I also had to repeatedly insist to obtain the biopsy and cytology results, which were never sent spontaneously.
The treatment was unsuccessful, the tests did not bring any solution, and in the end, only a very high bill remained without any improvement in the animal's health.
I spent a fortune to receive a cold, disorganized service marked by a lack of empathy.

I'm giving 1 star because it's not possible to give zero.

In short, we had a problem with our dog on December 22nd (a serious case of diarrhea) and we went to this hospital because, despite the terrible references we had, it was the only place available that day.

Analyzing point by point:
1) Veterinarian's service - I have to be fair and say that she is an excellent professional and was very attentive.

2) Reception service - the girls we interacted with are very, very, very bad, especially the one who attended to me today (December 31st). Today's receptionist proved to be extremely unprepared, rude, and lacking any emotional intelligence. She shouldn't be working in customer service at all.

3) Price - some tests and they already charged around 500 euros. An absurdly expensive price for such poor service/attention. The little chart they have at reception is useless because they add a bunch of things to your bill that aren't "covered" there.

Anyway, my wife and I had to ask for the test results several times, and only after going there in person today was I able to get the reports. A detail: I went there because I received terrible telephone service from one of the receptionists (who, unsurprisingly, appears in other complaints here on Google, also from customers complaining about the same thing – terrible service...).

The first surprise: the ultrasound report I requested 9 days ago was done on the spot, in 10 minutes by the veterinarian, because she saw that the deadline had already expired by 2 days. A detail: only then did they tell me that the deadline is 7 days and not "a few days" as had been previously mentioned. The second surprise: my dog's test results had been ready for two days, and even though I called to ask about them, I don't know if it was due to a lack of empathy or simply laziness on the part of the receptionist, but it was there, forgotten.

Note: Why the rush? Because my dog ​​is sick and I need to be sure she doesn't have anything more serious than diarrhea. It makes absolutely no sense to have a test done and not have the results as quickly as possible.

I would definitely only return to this place if it were a matter of life or death because I refuse to pay so much to receive such poor and unempathetic service. I believe the only positive thing was the veterinarian, because otherwise, it was a terrible experience.
Nice Clinique overall. I would not say it’s the “best in the world” but everyone is competent and service is good, so I am greatful.
My 4-month-old kitten arrived at Anicura in very bad shape after falling from the 4th floor. He was hospitalized for 5 days and received excellent care. I highly recommend this veterinary hospital.

Usually we are going to different clinic, but it is a bit far and close at 19. So when today at 18:30 we realized that our cat has problems with making pee, at 18:32 we decided to call this clinic and 20 min later we were here. Registration and waiting at reception took around 15 min. So at 19 and something we were waiting in the cabinet.
At about 19:20 doctor took our cat for blood and urinary tests, 5 min later come back to us saying “we need to sedate her, she is aggressive”. Never happened before, the cat is completely friendly with everyone before, we even offer to come in to calm her, but the answer was “no no, we need to sedate, sign the paper”. Ok. Doctor came back with cat at 20:11 (I was on the call so I know exact time). But the paper with test results showing time 19:43. Then we wait for doctor to bring medicine another 15-20 minutes.
20:35 we are paying by card on reception 188€. After that they print a receipt. And what I see? Being charged almost double for consultation! Not 41€ for “not scheduled consultation” (which is already not cheap but ok, health is more important), but 79€ for “urgent consultation”! The only issue - everything started and even was done before 20:00 according to the papers! And their “urgent time” starts if you come after 20 (so we were informed during the phone call prior to the visit). On my question “what is this?” the answer was “oh, you have to wait a doctor, I can’t change it”.

Only at 21:10 (35 min waiting!) finally received money in cash back from same receptionist. Doctor never appeared. Felt like they were just waiting that we will “eat it” and go without getting money back.

More than 2 hours spent there, of which the procedure itself took max 25-30 min. The rest was waiting.
Total of 150€ for consultation(41)+blood tests(46,3)+meds for a week(40,7) and sedation(22). I’ve trusted good reviews, but unfortunately disappointed. Service/Price not matching. But they are open 24h and not far from home, hopefully won’t need that service.

Recommendation:
Insist on detailed receipt Before payment, and check it very carefully!!! Otherwise you might overpay without noticing or you gonna wait forever for getting your money back.

"Everything has a price"...
This phrase was said to me countless times when I simply asked for help because I was desperate about what was happening to my cat.
I am a minor, I am alone at home, and at 3 am I had to desperately go out looking for help because I simply asked someone to shave a super small part of my cat's fur because it had citronella candle wax stuck to it.
I went looking for a machine, so I could cut it myself, to my colleagues' houses, 4 hours of pure despair, and I was alone on the street in the middle of the night because of inhumane people. I don't wish this feeling on anyone, not even these people who had no consideration whatsoever.
€100 for a simple consultation, for shaving a simple 2/3cm area, I don't have that kind of money, but "Everything has a price"... let's think about whether this is a fair price for a simple task like this.
I truly hope nothing happens to my cat because I did everything I could, but I can't help but report this completely inhumane behavior, not to mention the arrogance of the woman who attended to me in the face of my desperation.

A great choice. My dog ​​had been without appetite and defecating for a week, and between clinics, exams, x-rays, and ultrasounds, they couldn't detect what was wrong with Noah... I decided to take her to the Porto Veterinary Hospital - AniCura (always with apprehension because the costs would be much higher), a choice that was undoubtedly the right one... a great hospital that works 24 hours a day without fail, from reception to veterinarians, veterinary nurses, veterinary assistants, etc... (Dr. Catarina and Dr. Maria João) were Noah's salvation. In less than 24 hours, they diagnosed Addison's disease, a chronic disease that, with medication and control, Noah can return to her normal life.

I advise anyone not to hesitate to go there... the prices are for normal consultations; what will be more expensive are the more specific exams.
On behalf of myself and Noah, we sincerely thank you for your daily work.

I recommend them for the care they provide to their animal patients ❤️
Excellent professionals

We speak English and struggle with Portuguese, so it is great to have a place which not only provides amazing care, but most of the staff speaks English!  In difficult times, it is even more stressful to try to speak another language, but at CHV, they make it easy!

Rufus had two back surgeries here. The first surgery went perfectly fine. The second surgery was as bad as it could get (not the hospitals fault).   But he’s still with us and after months of rehab, he’s still part of the family.

His care was only possible because to was a fraction of what it would have been in the USA. In the USA, for emergency surgery, a CAT scan, and 10 days in the hospital, we would have been looking between $25,000-$30,000.   Our bill was about 12-14% of that.

So, although not cheap, it would have been cost prohibited in the USA.

However, getting a phone call through to the hospital can be difficult, but they do respond to emails relatively well.

This is a 24 hour hospital, not a doctors office. After 8 PM, you will be billed at higher rates. For real emergencies, call or email before arriving to help move things faster.

Although Rufus hates being left behind, we visited every day and he’s about 15-20% of his younger self. No more jumping or walking more than a block, or stairs. He has a wagon.

Dr. Hugo is a professional unlike any I've ever seen. Attentive, efficient, and knowledgeable about what he does, and he does it with care and attention.
The hospital is impeccable, the entire team is fantastic. I wish all animals could be treated by this team. Thank you and I recommend them!

I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS HOSPITAL TO ANYONE WHO TRULY LOVES THEIR PET!

Since February 7th, I have been waiting for a response to my email from Dr. Hugo Gregório, the veterinarian responsible for this hospital, whom I thought was a responsible and honest professional. This is due not only to the horrible way they treated my Yorkie, but also to the extra money they charged on top of what I had already paid them at the time of hospitalization.

Apparently, this is common practice at this hospital, which leads me to consider filing a complaint about this frankly dishonest and, above all, very inhumane behavior with a higher authority!

If I had read the reviews before taking my Yorkie there, I probably would still have her alive with me!

INCOMPETENCE KILLS!!!!!

And because of this incompetence and an avid need to MAKE money at all costs, THEY KILLED MY YORKIE!!!!!
I am suffering terribly because of what they did and the inhumane way they handled the matter, apparently identical to many others already recorded in the reviews, which, unfortunately, I didn't read before going to the emergency room!

The emergency room works TERRIBLY!!
DO NOT ACCEPT THE NONSENSE THAT YOU CANNOT SEE YOUR PET SO AS NOT TO WORSEN ITS CONDITION!

Pyky would have been much calmer if they had let me see her after entering the emergency room!
They even fail at that!! LACK OF SENSITIVITY!!!!!!!!

They are more concerned with making a budget than with saving the animals that come in needing help.

They do not respect the need for the owner to be present in serious cases so that the pet does not suffer so much. They do not warn when they are very ill so that the owner can say goodbye and support them during this difficult time. They are exclusively concerned with the payment that exceeds the budget, half of which is paid as soon as our pet is admitted.

The reception staff are anything but well-trained and humane people to be in charge of a hospital.
My Yorkie died. None of them offered any condolences, they just told me I still had €79.00 to pay in addition to the €320.00 deposit I gave out of the €640.00 estimated for 3 days, 2 in intensive care and 1 in recovery.
My Yorkie was only in this "hospital" for 12 hours. She wasn't lethargic. She was walking perfectly. She ate, she drank... she had pneumonia being treated with antibiotics. In the emergency room, the veterinarian Ana Freitas didn't even tell me she was at risk of dying. She was only concerned about whether or not I would pay the estimate she would have to make while the little one was inside...
The next morning... She passed away without them calling me to tell me she wasn't recovering and without giving me the opportunity to comfort her at the time of her passing. Not even her blanket was with her, something I asked for and left in the emergency room so they wouldn't feel abandoned. It was just to give her oxygen and stabilize her! NOTHING MORE!

Where is the care and concern for pets?

Yesterday, when I finally mustered the strength to speak with the doctor who was treating her, Dr. Hugo Gregório, one of the receptionists couldn't answer my request to explain why there were additional charges on top of what had already been paid and replied that I had to ask the doctor. Another one, a certain Sara Antunes, after I said I was disappointed by the lack of care, only concerned with presenting bills and not even offering condolences after the pet's death at that hospital, responded in a rude, sarcastic, unprofessional, and inhumane tone towards a client of this "hospital" who had just lost her pet: "Congratulations!" And she laughed! What left everyone who witnessed it embarrassed by so much insensitivity and lack of training!
